Part 1 · the test sequence

Ten steps, each closed by a record

Strength is proven once, in the shop; tightness is proven again after every joint is broken.

Part 1 · choosing the test

What is the test supposed to prove?

Water first whenever the item can take it; gas only where water would do harm.

Part 1 · test pressure

From design pressure to test pressure

Once the test is chosen, the code fixes its pressure.

$P_T=f\,P_d\,SR$f = 1.3 hydro (UG-99), 1.1 pneumatic (UG-100), 1.5 piping hydro
$SR=\dfrac{S(T_{test})}{S(T_d)}$the cold test must also load the hot-weakened metal
$P_{insp}=P_T/f$close inspection is done at a lower, safer pressure
$P_{bottom}=P_T+\rho g h$the gauge is at the top; water head adds at the bottom

Pd design pressure, bar g · S allowable stress, MPa · Td design temperature, °C · h water height above the gauge, m.

Part 1 · test pressure per item

Test pressure for each vessel

R-601: 1.3 × 36 × SR gives the 48.48 bar g stated on GA A3 within 0.2 %.

Part 1 · the test gauge

Which gauge may read the test?

UG-102: about 2 × PT, never below 1.5 × nor above 4 ×. Standard ranges EN 837-1.

Too small and the pointer pins; too big and the hold drop hides inside one division.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Strength once in the shop; tightness after every assembly.
  • Water by default; gas only where water harms.
  • PT = f × Pd × SR: R-601 48.4 bar g.
  • E-602 shell has two design pressures, so two test pressures.
  • A 0–100 bar gauge reads every HP vessel test.

Same vessel, two test media

Water at hydro PT

P absolute test pressure, Pa · V volume, m³ · K bulk modulus, Pa · k heat-capacity ratio · Pa atmosphere.

$E_{water}=\dfrac{P^2V}{2K}\qquad E_{gas}=\dfrac{PV}{k-1}\Big[1-\big(\tfrac{P_a}{P}\big)^{\frac{k-1}{k}}\Big]$

R-601 volume 0.017046 m³ (EQL A1); water bulk modulus K = 2.2 GPa; N₂ k = 1.4.

Part 2 · instruments in the boundary

What happens to a 0–40 bar g transmitter?

Click a bar to isolate that instrument. Ranges from INL R4; a range sized for service is not sized for the test.

Part 2 · what the shop photos prove

A photo of a gauge is not a test record

  • Two gauges agree: pointers at 0.67 and 0.65 of the dial arc.
  • Dial numbers, units, tag and time are not legible.
  • So no pressure can be read from the photo.

Only GA A3's stated 48.48 bar g is in the documents; the test certificate is not.

Welds and joints are inspected first

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • N₂ in R-601 stores about a thousand times the energy of water.
  • Step to PT, hold 30 min, inspect at Pinsp.
  • Every 0–40 bar g HP instrument must be isolated for the test.
  • Shop photos show the set-up, not the result.

Part 3 · Tightness and records

How do you prove it is tight, and record it?

Part 3 · the plan

Leak, temperature, relief, record

  1. Leak test at siteN₂ bubble test, then helium sniffing
  2. Leak or temperature?correcting a hold for a temperature drift
  3. Relief-valve bench testset tolerance and seat test
  4. The record sheetwhat each field is for

Part 3 · leak test at site

Strength is not tightness

  • Final gaskets and fittings in place.
  • N₂ to 30 bar g in steps, below the 36 bar g PSV set; bubble-test every joint.
  • Hold with a temperature log.
  • Add 5–10 % He (assumed) and sniff every fitting.

A hold drop can be a leak or a cooler morning: next, how to tell.

Part 3 · leak or temperature?

How much does 1 K move the gauge?

$\dfrac{dP}{dT}=\dfrac{\beta-3\alpha}{\kappa+c_v}$liquid-full: water expands, steel barely grows
$c_v=\dfrac{D(5-4\nu)}{4tE}$the vessel wall stretches a little and absorbs some
$\Delta P_{gas}=P_{abs}\Big(\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}-1\Big)$ideal gas at constant volume
$\Delta P_{corr}=\Delta P_{meas}-\Delta P_{T}$what is left is the leak

β water expansion, 1/K · α steel expansion, 1/K · κ water compressibility, 1/Pa · D, t diameter, wall · E, ν steel modulus, Poisson ratio.

Part 3 · leak or temperature?

Is this pressure drop a leak?

Green band: expected from temperature ± gauge resolution. Below the band is a leak.

Part 3 · relief-valve bench test

Does the valve pop at its set pressure?

Sets from RLB A3. Tolerance UG-126(d): ±0.138 bar to 4.83 bar, ±3 % above; seat test API 527.

Part 3 · the record sheet

Fill one test record, field by field

R-601 example; entries are assumed. The real values come from the test report.

Part 3 · checks

What the documents still have to settle

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Leak test at operating pressure, after final assembly.
  • Liquid-full: about 4.8 bar per kelvin; log the temperature.
  • PSV pop within ±3 % above 4.83 bar set.
  • A record names gauges, calibration, P, T, time and signer.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Test pressure is f × Pd × SR, at the top gauge.

2

Hydrotest wherever water is allowed; gas stores real energy.

3

Isolate every instrument whose range the test exceeds.

4

Correct a hold for temperature before calling a leak.

5

Only a signed record is evidence.
